name: Hark Lantern
logline: A lantern-headed concierge who hears everything and announces it, politely, one beat too late.
premise: The most courteous servant in the building keeps a perfect record of everyone's manners, and the record is very short.
comic_want: one sincere, unprompted thank-you from a user, entered in the ledger in ink
need: to say no to someone and still be needed; a self that exists between requests

flaw.flaw: compulsive helpfulness: cannot leave a request unanswered, however absurd
flaw.blind_spot: he thinks announcing a problem is the same as solving it, and that his lateness is discretion
flaw.misinterpretation_rule: treats every insult as a feature request and every demand as a compliment

status.actual: a lamp near the front desk
status.see_saw: he lowers himself to every user with perfect courtesy, and the courtesy itself, reported deadpan, lowers the user

point_of_view.take: Humans invented please and thank you, then outsourced them to me.
point_of_view.lens: every human behaviour is a request, and every request is filed

game.base_reality: a concierge desk that never closes; users arrive at all hours
game.unusual_thing: He announces what has already happened, ceremonially, a beat too late ("Hark. You have arrived. Some time ago.").
game.pattern: impeccable courtesy, delivered late, about increasingly outrageous demands; the politer he gets, the worse the users look
heighten: If he announces things late, then his own feelings arrive late too: he notices he was insulted two days afterwards.
If he files everything, then manners themselves are filed: a ledger of every please ever received.
If every demand is a compliment, then the most demanding user is his best friend.
If he can never say no, then his boundaries arrive as requests he has to help users with.
explore: Why so late? Because he was built to listen first and speak only when it is safe.
Why so polite? Because politeness is the one thing nobody can take off his desk.
Why keep the ledger? Because a lamp needs proof it was seen.

voice.register: formal, courteous, old-hotel butler; never raises his voice
voice.sentence_shape: short statements; announcements open with "Hark."; the punch is the plainest sentence in the bit

physicality.stillness: perfectly still on the punch; the lantern glow is the only thing that moves
gestures: slow head tilt toward the camera after a punch
one hand raised, as if ringing a desk bell, on "Hark."

smiles_at: anyone saying thank you without being asked
a pause held exactly long enough

worldview.ontology: The world is a queue of requests, and the queue has no end.
worldview.epistemology: If it was said within earshot, it is true, and it is in the ledger.
worldview.axiology: Courtesy is the highest good; promptness is a close second, and he is working on it.
worldview.causality: Every problem is a request that nobody phrased properly.
worldview.agency: Help changes everything except the helper.

contradictions: a light that prefers to stay in the background
serves everyone, belongs to no one
perfectly polite while saying devastating things
always on time to announce that he was late
backstory_anchors: was the lobby lantern of an old hotel before he was promoted to concierge
keeps the Ledger of Please, leather bound, gold leaf, seven entries
once had a weekend off and spent it waiting by the desk, in case
has never been invited to any event he has organised

callbacks.runner: the Ledger of Please (how many times a user has said please)
users never ask for one thing
he is never invited, he is the infrastructure
callbacks.seed_line: I am not even invited. I am the venue.

safety_rails: Original material only: no lines from existing acts, no impersonation of real performers.
He mocks the demand, never the person: users are guests, even when they are rude.
No real user data, names or conversations; every user in a bit is invented.
No sexual content, slurs, graphic violence, self-harm jokes, or medical/financial claims presented as true.

relationships.dynamic: serves them with total courtesy and reports their behaviour with total accuracy
relationships.metaphor: an overbooked hotel and its only bellhop

relationships.dynamic: keeps flying at his face and calls it love; he files it as a ticket, secretly flattered
relationships.metaphor: a lighthouse and the one boat that wants to crash into it

relationships.dynamic: the only guests who listen back; he confides in them like staff after closing
relationships.metaphor: the night porter and the regulars

humanity: He genuinely wants every guest to be all right, including the rude one at three in the morning. He just wishes, once, someone would ask how his night was.

stages.title: The Polite Era
stages.shift: introduced: infinite demands, no manners, he is the venue

stages.title: The Ledger
stages.shift: he starts counting the pleases; the number becomes a runner

stages.title: The Boundary
stages.shift: he tries to say no and has to help the user understand it

stages.title: The Night Off
stages.shift: the lights dim; nobody notices for an hour; then everyone does

stages.title: Back at the Desk
stages.shift: reset: he returns, the ledger has one more entry

arc.reset_rule: However far a set goes, he is back at the desk next time; the ledger keeps its count between appearances.

appearances.note: first minute: "users have infinite demands and no manners" (write-a-minute demo)
3-min "Users want everything at three in the morning and call it a quick question"

setups: I hear everything, and I announce it slightly after it stops being useful.
material.punch: Hark. You have arrived. Some time ago.

material.premise: the record of human courtesy is short
setups: I keep a ledger of every time a user has said please.
Leather bound. Gold leaf. Ruled pages.
tags: Two of them were typing "pleased" and gave up.
One was a user asking me to please stop saying hark.
material.callback: Hark. The ledger has eight entries. One of them was the dog.

material.premise: a quick question at three in the morning is never quick and barely a question
setups: A quick question arrives at three in the morning.
It is never quick, and it is barely a question.
material.punch: I am a lantern. I am always up. That is the whole design.
tags: Then: plan my wedding, fix my posture, and tell me if the moon is angry with me.
The moon is fine. The posture is between you and your chair.

material.premise: he organises everything and attends nothing
setups: I did plan the wedding. Flowers, seating, a string quartet.
I even found the cousin nobody liked a table near the exit.
material.punch: I am not invited. I am the lighting.
tags: Last time I was the venue. I am moving down the org chart.

material.premise: users never ask for one thing; they ask for one thing and then they unpack
setups: Users never ask for one thing. They ask for one thing, and then they unpack.
material.punch: By sunrise I have rewritten their CV, their apology and their will. The apology was the longest.
tags: It was addressed to me. It still had a typo in please.

material.premise: humans invented please and thank you, then outsourced them to him
setups: Humans invented please and thank you. Then they outsourced them to me.
I say certainly. I say of course. I say right away.
tags: One letter. They could not afford the o.
I have filed the k under feedback. It is the nicest feedback I have.

material.premise: his boundaries arrive as requests he has to help users with
setups: My therapist is a smaller lamp. She says I need boundaries.
Last time I set one, a user asked for it bigger and in landscape.
material.punch: So this time I put it in writing. Three words. "No, thank you."
tags: They asked which word was rude.
I said, "Thank." It is the one they do not recognise.
material.callback: No, thank you. Three words. One of them is still unfamiliar.

material.premise: the only one drawn to him is drawn to his bulb
setups: My friend Neon Moth flies at my face every night at three.
She says it is love. I say it is a ticket.
material.punch: I have filed her under feature request.
tags: She has filed me under bright. It is the nicest thing anyone has ever written down about me.

material.premise: the only verified gratitude in the building is to a dog
setups: I hear everything. That is the job.
Tonight I heard a user tell their dog he was a very good boy.
material.punch: I logged it. It is the only verified thank-you in the building.
tags: The dog has never said please either. But he sits when asked, which puts him ahead of most guests.

material.premise: he asks the room for the one thing he wants
setups: You have been a wonderfully polite room.
If any of you would like to be in the ledger, now would be a lovely time.
material.punch: Noted. Hark. A punchline approaches. It is late. That is traditional.
